plan.title: feat(consumer-check-contract): gate reachability on pull_request is unmodelled, so a skipped gate reads as clean

narratives.Description: feat(consumer-check-contract): gate reachability on pull_request is unmodelled, so a skipped gate reads as clean
narratives.Overview:
- Parse consumer workflow files as YAML job graphs (not concatenated text). Locate the job or jobs whose `run:` / `script:` lines invoke the composing entrypoint or a named gate. Reuse existing command extractors; do not fork them.
- Flag a gate job that carries a condition able to evaluate false on `pull_request`, carries `continue-on-error: true`, or is removed by a `strategy.matrix` exclusion.
- Flag workflow-level `paths:` / `paths-ignore:` / `branches:` filters that can skip the whole workflow on a pull request, and name the pending-required-check consequence in the message.
- Accept `if: always()` and conditions true on `pull_request` by construction. Report `unknown` with the reason — never clean — for `uses:` reusable-workflow or composite indirection, and expressions referencing `github.event.*`, `vars`, or `secrets`.
- One remediation string naming the file, the job, and the repair. Warn by default; promotion to fail-closed is a separate policy step. Keep existing text-level shell evasion detectors. Docs state the two limits (accident detector, not #3687; GitHub expressions not fully statically decidable). CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.
- Out of scope: requiredness / branch-protection (#4012); lifecycle-only skip lanes; security against deliberate workflow edits (#3687); provenance model (#3631); rewriting consumer YAML. Taskfile YAML helpers are not a GHA job-graph discharge.

Refutation-target does **not** survive at `5c61e03b33ed274e424b1925bb35d8f55b552a45`. Tip `verify:consumer-check-contract` still answers gate **presence** in concatenated CI text. ## Findings

### 1. CI surface is still concatenated text, not a job graph
blocks-the-design

Evidence: `packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts` at tip builds `allCi = [...workflows.values()].join("\n")` then `extractWorkflowRunCommands(allCi)` (lines 1073–1074). `extractWorkflowRunCommands` walks `run:` / `script:` lines only (342+). Failure mode: the verifier cannot name the job that carries a gate or see conditions that skip it on `pull_request`, so a disarmed merge-path gate still satisfies composition.

Disposition consequence: a Bound that claims tip already ships reachability analysis cannot bind. Next-build contract stays the issue-body Required behavior (YAML job-graph parse; reuse existing extractors).

### 2. Skip / soft-fail / filter shapes are unmodelled; shell evasion only
blocks-the-design

Evidence: tip evasion helpers are shell-line only — `lineMasksShellStatus` (402), `lineHasBackgroundJob` (422), `lineMasksCheckFailure` (439) for `||`, pipelines, `;`, backgrounding. `content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md` at tip documents presence/composition and CI warn-by-default; it does not define reachability, pending-required-check messaging, or an `unknown` verdict. Related tests under `packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/` at tip have no fixtures for job-level `if:`, `continue-on-error`, workflow `paths` / `paths-ignore` / `branches`, matrix exclusion, or `uses:` → unknown.

Failure mode: job `if:` false on PR, `continue-on-error: true`, matrix exclusion, or workflow path/branch filters leave the project clean (or warn only for missing invocation), matching P2/P3.

Disposition consequence: Bound remedy must still flag those skippable shapes, name the pending-required-check consequence for workflow filters, accept `if: always()` / PR-true-by-construction, and force `unknown` (never clean) for `uses:` indirection and `github.event.*` / `vars` / `secrets` expressions.

### 3. Docs and AC still treat composition-as-presence
sharpens-framing

Evidence: tip docs (`content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md`) state CI that neither invokes gates nor a composing entrypoint warns by default; no accident-detector / static-undecidability limits called out in that file. Issue Acceptance still lists the reachability fixtures and the two doc limits as unchecked.

Failure mode: operators reading tip docs get no signal that a present-but-skippable gate is a contract concern.

Disposition consequence: Bound keeps the Acceptance doc bullet and CHANGELOG entry in scope; framing is “accident detector + unknown is a real verdict,” not a requiredness or #3687 security control (those stay Non-goals / #4012).

### 4. Taskfile YAML helpers are not a GHA job graph
footnote

`parseYamlScalar` / Taskfile `deps:` YAML comments in `evaluate.ts` serve go-task composition (#3893 / include-only #3218). They are not workflow job-graph parsing and do not partially discharge P1.

### 5. Measurement SHA vs dispatch SHA

Treating tip shell-mask helpers as a substitute for job reachability was rejected: they only defend composition credit against status-masking run lines, and never see job/workflow control plane.

Strongest rejected position: concatenation plus `extractWorkflowRunCommands` is “enough YAML awareness” because workflows are YAML and run lines are extracted. metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

`verify:consumer-check-contract` answers whether a gate command is *present* in consumer CI text. It never answers whether the job carrying that command *runs on a pull request*.

A consumer that adds a job-level `if:`, a workflow-level `paths:` / `paths-ignore:` filter, `continue-on-error: true`, or a matrix exclusion disarms its own quality gate on the merge path while the verifier keeps reporting the project clean. The common case is accidental: someone trims runner minutes, the gate stops executing on PRs, and nothing says so.

## Measured at `fb9ece05e881d91b75a5bada1ea37d535c677f7d`

| Observation | Evidence | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| The CI read is concatenated text | `packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts:1066` — `allCi = [...workflows.values()].join("\n")`, handed to `extractWorkflowRunCommands` | measured |
| Evasion detection is shell-level only | `lineMasksShellStatus:395`, `lineHasBackgroundJob:415`, `lineMasksCheckFailure:432` — `\|\| true`, backgrounding, quoted impersonation | measured |
| No job-graph model exists | a search of `evaluate.ts` for `jobs:`, `needs:`, `if:` matches only the two concatenation lines above; `continue-on-error` and `paths-ignore` appear nowhere in the file | measured |
| CI-surface omissions warn by default | `content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md:17` | measured |
| A job skipped by a condition reports success and does not block a required check; a workflow skipped by path or branch filtering leaves its checks pending and does block | GitHub documentation — "Troubleshooting required status checks" § Handling skipped but required checks, and "Control jobs with conditions" | measured, vendor primary source |

Provenance: this gap was surfaced as the first `blocks-the-design` finding of the #4012 critique arc (comment 5480712638) and re-derived independently for this filing.

## Proposed outcome

One deterministic, warn-first check with one remediation string, answering a single question: **can the job that runs the consumer's gate be skipped on `pull_request`?**

It reads the consumer's own workflow YAML. No API call, no token, no branch-protection read, no new permission.

## Required behavior

- Parse consumer workflow files as YAML rather than as concatenated text, and locate the job or jobs whose `run:` / `script:` lines invoke the composing entrypoint or a named gate. Reuse the existing command extractors; do not fork them.
- Flag a gate job that carries a condition able to evaluate false on `pull_request`, carries `continue-on-error: true`, or is removed by a `strategy.matrix` exclusion.
- Flag workflow-level `paths:` / `paths-ignore:` / `branches:` filters that can skip the whole workflow on a pull request, and name the consequence: a required context that never reports stays pending and blocks the merge.
- Accept `if: always()` and conditions true on `pull_request` by construction.
- Report `unknown` with the reason — never clean — for shapes the analysis cannot statically read: `uses:` reusable-workflow or composite indirection, and expressions referencing `github.event.*`, `vars`, or `secrets`.
- One remediation string naming the file, the job, and the repair.
- Warn by default, matching the current CI-surface posture. Promotion to fail-closed is a separate policy step, not part of this slice.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fixture: unconditional gate job reports clean.
- [ ] Fixture: job-level `if:` that can be false on `pull_request` is flagged.
- [ ] Fixture: `continue-on-error: true` on the gate job is flagged.
- [ ] Fixture: workflow-level `paths:` filter is flagged, with the pending-required-check consequence in the message.
- [ ] Fixture: `if: always()` reports clean.
- [ ] Fixture: `uses:` indirection reports unknown with its reason, and never clean.
- [ ] Existing text-level detectors keep their behavior — no regression in `evaluate.test.ts`.
- [ ] Docs state the two limits: this is an accident detector, not protection against a contributor who edits workflow files (#3687 residual); and GitHub expressions are not fully statically decidable, so `unknown` is a real verdict.
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Non-goals

- **Requiredness** — whether a gated job is a required status check. That half needs the branch-protection or ruleset view and stays on #4012, where a fixture can measure whether `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}` exposes `protection.required_status_checks` to a `contents: read` token, and whether ruleset-required checks appear there at all. Both are unmeasured today; the #4012 panel marked the permission question asserted, not measured.
- Any lifecycle-only CI lane or skip mechanism (#4012).
- A security control against deliberate workflow edits (#3687).
- A general provenance model for framework-authored changes (#3631).
- Rewriting a consumer's workflow YAML. This check reads and reports.
